learning_goals: Convert between particles, moles, and mass using Avogadro's constant and molar mass.
Determine empirical or molecular formulas from percent composition and molar mass.
Use balanced equations to solve stoichiometric product and reactant problems.
Interpret simple lab data to calculate theoretical yield and percent yield.
Show organized chemical work with correct units and significant digits.

source_files.notes: Curated from the clean text extraction of the printed Unit 3 stoichiometry test.

observed_patterns: The source is a one-page SCH3U Unit 3 stoichiometry paper with 7 constructed-response questions.
Questions 1 to 3 assess particle-mole-mass conversions and amount reasoning.
Question 4 requires percent composition analysis leading to a molecular formula.
Questions 5 and 6 are balanced-equation stoichiometry problems, with question 6 explicitly requiring a balanced equation before mass calculation.
Question 7 is a percent-yield lab problem using precipitate mass and filter-paper data.
Marks are concentrated in multi-step stoichiometry and lab-yield reasoning, for a total of 35 marks.
inferred_patterns: The teacher expects all work to be shown with units, formulas, and significant digits.
The paper intentionally ramps from single-concept conversions into multi-step stoichiometry and lab analysis.
Fresh versions should preserve the exact skill spread and mark balance without copying the original numbers or compounds verbatim.

analysis_summary.notes: This curated blueprint replaces the under-specified heuristic version and preserves the source paper's complete stoichiometry structure.

sections.title: Foundational Stoichiometry Calculations
sections.instructions: Show all work. Include units and use appropriate significant digits.

sections.title: Composition and Reaction Stoichiometry
sections.instructions: Show a complete stoichiometric setup. Write and balance any required chemical equation before solving.

sections.title: Lab Yield Analysis
sections.instructions: Use the data provided to determine theoretical yield and percent yield. Show your setup clearly.

ordering_rules: Move into longer multi-step composition and reaction calculations.
Finish with a lab-style percent-yield analysis question.

progression_notes: The test should escalate from one-step conversions into multi-step stoichiometric setups.
The heaviest-mark questions should require equation balancing, mole-ratio reasoning, and interpretation of lab measurements.

trap_patterns.description: Students may forget to divide by Avogadro's constant or may mix atoms, molecules, and formula units.
examples: Using molar mass when converting formula units to moles
Counting atoms instead of molecules without accounting for subscripts

trap_patterns.description: Students may use incorrect molar masses or drop units during conversion steps.
examples: Incomplete molar mass calculation for polyatomic compounds

trap_patterns.description: Stoichiometric mole ratios fail if the reaction is not balanced first.
examples: Solving product mass without balancing the equation

trap_patterns.description: Students may confuse empirical formula steps with molecular formula scaling.
examples: Using percent values directly as subscripts

trap_patterns.description: Lab questions require separating precipitate mass from filter-paper mass before computing percent yield.
examples: Using combined mass as actual yield
Reversing actual and theoretical yield in the percent-yield formula

section_1.stem: Calculate the amount of substance in moles for 7.22 x 10^23 formula units of zinc phosphate, Zn3(PO4)2(s).
Calculate the mass of 0.415 mol of aluminum sulfate, Al2(SO4)3(s).
How many hydrogen atoms are present in 0.750 mol of ammonia, NH3(g)?

section_2.stem: A compound is 52.2% carbon, 13.1% hydrogen, and 34.7% oxygen by mass. Its molar mass is 92.1 g/mol. Determine the molecular formula of the compound.
section_2.answer_hint: Empirical formula C2H6O; molecular formula C4H12O2

section_2.stem: In excess chlorine gas, iron reacts to form iron(III) chloride. Calculate the mass of FeCl3(s) produced when 11.2 g of iron is used.

Phosphoric acid reacts with calcium hydroxide to produce calcium phosphate and water. If 6.50 g of H3PO4(aq) reacts completely with excess Ca(OH)2(aq), what mass of Ca3(PO4)2(s) is produced? Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction.

section_3.stem: Use the lab data below to determine the percentage yield of silver chloride, AgCl(s), produced when excess sodium chloride is added to silver nitrate solution. Lab data: mass of AgNO3 used = 1.62 g; mass of clean, dry filter paper = 1.14 g; mass of dry precipitate and filter paper = 2.48 g. Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction.
section_3.answer_hint: AgNO3 + NaCl -> AgCl + NaNO3; actual precipitate mass = 1.34 g; theoretical yield is about 1.37 g AgCl; percentage yield is about 98.0%

section_1.stem: Calculate the amount of substance in moles for 5.41 x 10^22 formula units of calcium nitrate, Ca(NO3)2(s).
Calculate the mass of 1.20 mol of potassium phosphate, K3PO4(s).
How many oxygen atoms are present in 2.25 mol of sulfur dioxide, SO2(g)?

section_2.stem: A compound is 48.6% carbon, 8.16% hydrogen, and 43.2% oxygen by mass. Its molar mass is 74.1 g/mol. Determine the molecular formula of the compound.
section_2.answer_hint: Empirical formula C3H6O2; molecular formula C3H6O2

section_2.stem: In excess oxygen, phosphorus reacts to form tetraphosphorus decoxide, P4O10(s). Calculate the mass of P4O10 produced when 6.20 g of P4(s) is used.
section_2.answer_hint: 14.2 g P4O10 approximately after using P4 + 5O2 -> P4O10

section_2.stem: Sulfuric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide to produce sodium sulfate and water. If 4.90 g of H2SO4(aq) reacts completely with excess NaOH(aq), what mass of Na2SO4(s) is produced? Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction.

section_3.stem: Use the lab data below to determine the percentage yield of lead(II) iodide, PbI2(s), produced when excess potassium iodide is added to lead(II) nitrate solution. Lab data: mass of Pb(NO3)2 used = 1.36 g; mass of clean, dry filter paper = 1.08 g; mass of dry precipitate and filter paper = 2.50 g. Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction.
section_3.answer_hint: Pb(NO3)2 + 2KI -> PbI2 + 2KNO3; actual precipitate mass = 1.42 g; theoretical yield is about 1.89 g PbI2; percentage yield is about 75.1%
